## Setup trajectory

Use the `amt` package to create a trajectory object from the cleaned data.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-summary="Create a trajectory object"}
pig_all <- pig_gps_cols %>% mk_track(id = id,
                                           lon,
                                           lat, 
                                           time, 
                                           all_cols = T,
                                           crs = 4326) %>% 
  transform_coords(crs_to = 3112, crs_from = 4326) # Transformation to GDA94 / 
# Geoscience Australia Lambert (https://epsg.io/3112)

pig_all <- pig_all %>% arrange(id, t_)

# plot the data spatially coloured by ID
pig_all %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x_, y = y_, colour = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) + 
  coord_fixed() +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  theme_classic()
```

## Creating a step object


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# nest the data by individual
pig_all_nested <- pig_all %>% arrange(id) %>% nest(data = -"id")

pig_all_nested_steps <- pig_all_nested %>%
  mutate(steps = map(data, function(x)
    x %>% track_resample(rate = minutes(30), tolerance = minutes(65)) %>%
      steps_by_burst(keep_cols = "start")))

# unnest the data after creating 'steps' objects
pig_all_steps <- pig_all_nested_steps %>% 
  amt::select(id, steps) %>% 
  amt::unnest(cols = steps) %>% 
  relocate(c(name, n_sat), .before = id) %>% 
  mutate(dt_min = as.numeric(difftime(t2_, t1_, units = "mins")),
         dt_hour = as.numeric(difftime(t2_, t1_, units = "hours"))) %>% 
  filter(dt_min > 20)

hist(as.numeric(pig_all_steps$dt_min))
```

# Add covariates

## Time and season


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pig_all_steps <- pig_all_steps %>% 
  mutate(
    hour = hour(t1_) + minute(t1_)/60 + second(t1_)/3600,
    hour_round = hour(t1_),date = as_date(t1_),
    month = month(t1_),
    .after = dt_hour,
    season = case_when(
      month %in% c(11,12, 1, 2, 3, 4) ~ "wet",
      month %in% seq(5,10) ~ "dry"),
    season2 = case_when(
      month %in% c(5, 6, 7) ~ "early dry",
      month %in% c(8, 9, 10) ~ "late dry",
      month %in% c(11, 12, 1) ~ "early wet",
```

```{.r .cell-code}
  dplyr::select(-hm, -`Station Number`, -matches("quality", ignore.case = TRUE),
                -matches("Ceilometer"), -`AWS Flag`, -`#`) %>%
  # combine the date/time components, which are in local standard time (Darwin has no daylight saving)
  dplyr::mutate(
    datetime = lubridate::make_datetime(
      year = `Year Month Day Hour Minutes in YYYY`,
      month = as.integer(MM),
      day = as.integer(DD),
      hour = as.integer(HH24),
      min = as.integer(`MI format in Local standard time`),
      tz = "Australia/Darwin"),
    .before = 1) %>%
  dplyr::select(-`Year Month Day Hour Minutes in YYYY`, -MM, -DD, -HH24,
                -`MI format in Local standard time`) %>%
  # any_of() as the cloud columns aren't recorded at Oenpelli
  dplyr::rename(dplyr::any_of(weather_names)) %>%
  # rain in each half-hour - the since-9am total resets after the 9:00 reading, so group by
  # rain day (9:30 to 9:00 the next day) and subtract the previous reading
  dplyr::mutate(rain_day = lubridate::as_date(datetime - lubridate::minutes(570))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(rain_day) %>%
  # round to remove floating point error from the subtraction (gauge resolution is 0.2 mm)
  dplyr::mutate(rain_30min_mm = round(rain_since_9am_mm - dplyr::lag(rain_since_9am_mm, default = 0), 1),
                .after = rain_since_9am_mm) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-rain_day) %>%
  dplyr::rename_with(~ paste0("onpli_", .x))
```

```{.r .cell-code}
jabiru_weather <- jabiru_weather_full %>%
  dplyr::select(-hm, -`Station Number`, -matches("quality", ignore.case = TRUE),
                -`AWS Flag`, -`#`) %>%
  # combine the date/time components, which are in local standard time (Darwin has no daylight saving)
  dplyr::mutate(
    datetime = lubridate::make_datetime(
      year = `Year Month Day Hour Minutes in YYYY`,
      month = as.integer(MM),
      day = as.integer(DD),
      hour = as.integer(HH24),
      min = as.integer(`MI format in Local standard time`),
      tz = "Australia/Darwin"),
    .before = 1) %>%
  dplyr::select(-`Year Month Day Hour Minutes in YYYY`, -MM, -DD, -HH24,
                -`MI format in Local standard time`) %>%
  dplyr::rename(dplyr::all_of(weather_names)) %>%
  # cloud amounts are coded few < scattered < broken < overcast
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(starts_with("cloud_amount"),
                              ~ factor(.x, levels = c("FEW", "SCT", "BKN", "OVC"),
                                       labels = c("few", "scattered", "broken", "overcast"),
                                       ordered = TRUE))) %>%
  # rain in each half-hour - the since-9am total resets after the 9:00 reading, so group by
  # rain day (9:30 to 9:00 the next day) and subtract the previous reading
  dplyr::mutate(rain_day = lubridate::as_date(datetime - lubridate::minutes(570))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(rain_day) %>%
  # round to remove floating point error from the subtraction (gauge resolution is 0.2 mm)
  dplyr::mutate(rain_30min_mm = round(rain_since_9am_mm - dplyr::lag(rain_since_9am_mm, default = 0), 1),
                .after = rain_since_9am_mm) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-rain_day) %>%
  dplyr::rename_with(~ paste0("jabru_", .x))
```

### Apply recode to raster


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
lvls <- levels(landcover_rast)[[1]]
lvls <- merge(lvls, recode_df, by.x = "Veg_class", by.y = "old",
              all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)

# check that all the old classes have been recoded to a new class
lvls$new[is.na(lvls$new)] <- lvls$Veg_class[is.na(lvls$new)]

# one new ID per unique merged label
new_lab <- unique(lvls$new)
new_id  <- match(lvls$new, new_lab)

# strip the old categories, then substitute old ID -> new ID
r_num <- terra::deepcopy(landcover_rast)
levels(r_num) <- NULL
landcover_rast_merged <- terra::classify(r_num, cbind(lvls$ID, new_id))

# attach the merged labels
levels(landcover_rast_merged) <- data.frame(ID = seq_along(new_lab),
                                            Veg_class = new_lab)
```
